title: Widening binary16 to binary32 and narrowing back is the identity
statement: Let RNE denote roundNearestTiesToEven. For every value x of IEEE-754 binary16, SMT-LIB `(_ FloatingPoint 5 11)`, converting x to binary32 and converting the result back to binary16 -- both conversions under RNE -- yields x again: `((_ to_fp 5 11) RNE ((_ to_fp 8 24) RNE x)) = x`, where `=` is SMT-LIB equality on the FloatingPoint sort (one NaN value, +0 and -0 distinct). This is the property that makes a binary16 tensor safe to stage through a binary32 accumulator and read back.

formal.statement: (assert (= ((_ to_fp 5 11) RNE ((_ to_fp 8 24) RNE x)) x))

evidence.supports: The negation of formal.statement is unsatisfiable, so the round trip is the identity on every binary16 value.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run --release -q -p axeyum-bench --example smtcomp_cli -- --evidence artifacts/facts/smt2/neg-fp16-fp32-roundtrip-identity.smt2 | tail -1)" = unsat
evidence.notes: Ran 2026-08-14: `; evidence kind=unsat-drat certified=1 recheck=ok arena=ok ms=6409`, verdict `unsat`, 9.6s wall in a release build. `recheck=ok` is axeyum's own `check_drat` (RUP+RAT) re-checking the emitted refutation; `arena=ok` is `Evidence::check` against a fresh parse. Cross-checked independently: `z3 -smt2` reports `unsat` (0.1s) and `bitwuzla 0.9.1` reports `unsat` (0.1s).

evidence.supports: All 65536 binary16 encodings round-tripped through binary32 by LLVM's APFloat: zero values changed.
evidence.notes: Ran 2026-08-14, under a second. examined=65536 failures=0, sharing no code with axeyum's lowering. The same run also settles bfloat16 -> binary32 -> bfloat16 (2^16, zero failures) and fp8 E5M2 -> binary32 -> fp8 E5M2 (2^8, zero failures); those are neighbouring propositions, not this one. NaN is handled as SMT-LIB requires -- all NaN encodings are one value, so a NaN that returns with a different payload still counts as returning the same value; APFloat bit equality alone would have reported a spurious failure here.

provenance.established_by: fp-kernels lane; axeyum SMT front door (QF_FP -> fpa2bv -> CNF -> DRAT) plus an independent exhaustive LLVM-APFloat enumeration
provenance.source: authored here; the mixed-precision-training question stated as a proposition rather than tested by sampling.

prior_art.what: That conversion to a format with both greater precision and greater exponent range is exact, hence invertible.
prior_art.attribution: standard textbook attribution; this lane did not consult the primary source, and records the citation as the received one. Nothing in the evidence above depends on it -- binary32 having strictly more of both is checked here by enumeration, not assumed.

notes:
THE INTERESTING NEIGHBOUR IS THE ONE THAT FAILS. This fact holds because binary32 dominates binary16 on BOTH axes: 24 significand bits against 11, and an exponent range that strictly contains binary16's. Drop either domination and the property dies -- see F:fp16-bf16-roundtrip-not-identity, where bfloat16 has the wider range but only 8 significand bits, and 83.6% of binary16 values do not survive the trip. The pair is the point: "cast to a 16-bit format and back" is not one operation with one answer, and which 16-bit format is chosen decides it.

ROUTE. `smt-clausal`, not `smt-term-level`: axeyum returned a DRAT refutation through CNF and re-checked it. The input domain is only 16 bits, but the fpa2bv lowering of a widen-then-narrow miter is far past the 20-bit `TERM_LEVEL_CERT_BITS` budget, so axeyum's own exhaustive-evaluation certificate is not available. The exhaustive route in the second evidence row is LLVM's APFloat, deliberately not axeyum's IR evaluator.

SCOPE. Exhaustive at binary16: every one of the 2^16 inputs was enumerated, and the solver route settles the same 2^16 symbolically. No claim is made for any other pair of formats.
